title: Mitigating Cost Impact on Customers with Beverage Container Return Scheme's Roll-out in April 2026
what_it_is: Mitigating Cost Impact on Customers with Beverage Container Return Scheme's Roll-out in April 2026

sections.label: Beverage Container Return Scheme questions
sections.summary: Questions ask about reverse vending machine numbers, redemption capacity, unredeemed deposits, and affordability impact on lower-income households before the April 2026 launch.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) how many operational reverse vending machines and return points will be available at the onset of the Beverage Container Return Scheme on 1 April 2026; (b) how will adequate capacity for redemption of deposits be assured during the roll-out of the scheme; and (c) how will unredeemed deposits be managed with full transparency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment given that the Beverage Container Return Scheme is projected to add 25 to 60 cents to prices of bottled and canned drinks of which only 10 cents is refundable, what assessment was made of the affordability impact on lower-income households before confirming the April 2026 launch.

sections.label: Ten-cent refundable deposit
sections.summary: All regulated beverage containers supplied in Singapore will attract a 10-cent deposit that is fully refundable.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: All regulated beverage containers supplied in Singapore will attract a 10-cent deposit, which is fully refundable.

sections.label: Producer fee per container
sections.summary: All producers must pay a producer fee of three to four cents per container to scheme operator BCRS Ltd.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: All producers will also need to pay a producer fee of three to four cents per container to the scheme operator, BCRS Ltd.

sections.label: Extended transition period and grant
sections.summary: The transition period was extended from three to six months, and a $2,500 transition grant was introduced for smaller businesses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Responding to feedback from producers that they needed more time to comply with the scheme requirements, we have extended the transition period from three months, to six months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We also introduced a transition grant of $2,500 to help smaller businesses.

sections.label: Scheme launch and transition support
sections.summary: Deposit-marked containers enter the market gradually, with widespread availability expected by August and September, and ambassadors deployed at launch.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: While the scheme officially starts in April, containers bearing the deposit mark will gradually enter the market during the transition period, with widespread availability expected by August and September.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: During this initial period, we will closely monitor return patterns and gather community feedback to determine the optimal location for these additional return points.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: At launch, we will deploy ambassadors on the ground to guide the public on how to use the RVMs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: NEA and BCRS Ltd, together with our community partners, are committed to providing additional support to better address their needs.

sections.label: Reverse vending machine logistics
sections.summary: Return point network operators contract companies to empty reverse vending machines at least once daily, and more if return rates are high.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: On the first matter, the RVMs are operated by the return point network operators.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: They have entered into contractual arrangements with companies to then do the reverse logistics – to empty out the RVMs at least once per day, and more if there is a high return rate at that particular machine.

sections.label: Producer container cost
sections.summary: Producers of 80% of beverage containers put to market say their cost is about three to four cents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: For 80% of the beverage containers that are put to market, the producers of these 80% of the containers have told us that their cost for doing so is about three to four cents.

sections.label: NEA watching beverage prices
sections.summary: NEA will watch beverage prices closely after the scheme is introduced and through the transition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Nevertheless, NEA will be watching the beverage prices after we introduce this scheme and through the transition, very closely.

sections.label: RVM queues and malfunctions
sections.summary: Questions ask about queues at RVMs and logistical arrangements for malfunctions, with 1,000 RVMs deployed first.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Given that everyone who buys a can will have to return the can to the vending machine to get back to 10 cents, do we anticipate queues and long waiting periods at the RVMs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And also, have we taken into consideration of the logistical arrangements in terms of malfunctions or that sort of operational challenges with the RVMs?

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We are deploying 1,000 RVMs in the first instance.

sections.label: RVM numbers and licensing
sections.summary: Assessed 1,000 to 2,000 RVMs are needed, with malfunctions and logistics part of licensing and contracts requiring 90% up-time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, we are taking those lessons in and through all of that, we have assessed that we do not need 15,000 RVMs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: There is a certain minimum volume collection per day that makes the logistical arrangements cost-effective, and we think that number is much closer to the 1,000 to 2,000 RVMs we are planning to have.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Addressing malfunctions and making logistical arrangements are part of licensing requirements for BCRS Ltd, and contractual arrangements that they have with their return point network operators and vendors of their machines.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: There is a contractual requirement for these machines to maintain 90% up-time.

sections.label: Smaller producer costs
sections.summary: For producers under 50,000 containers yearly, $2,500 covers registration and first-year producer fees of about $2,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: For a smaller producer, which we define as less than 50,000 beverage containers put to market per year, and that represents about one quarter of the producers in our estimate, the $2,500 is more than sufficient to cover both the product registration cost as well as the producer fees for the first year, which is about $2,000 in total.

sections.label: Market price increase
sections.summary: Assessment is that 80% of the market will have a 3% to 4% increase.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Our assessment is that 80% of the market will have a 3% to 4% increase.

sections.label: Refund methodology and cash
sections.summary: EZ-Link SimplyGo is a refund methodology and more will come, but cash or cash vouchers are not planned.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: For the refund methodology, we have explained that EZ-Link SimplyGo is available as a refund methodology and there will be further refund methodologies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We are not, at this point, planning for cash or cash voucher as forms of refund.

sections.label: Collusion and profiteering reporting
sections.summary: Mechanisms exist to report and deal with evidence of collusion or profiteering.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: If there is evidence of collusion or profiteering, there are mechanisms for that to be reported and dealt with.

sections.label: Grant amount and consumer impact
sections.summary: The passage asks whether consumer impact was factored into setting the grant at $2,500, citing choice and market functioning as protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And was this consumer impact factored into the decision to set the grant at only $2,500?

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: That availability of choice and the functioning of the market are likely to be the biggest protection.
